web:95028705b6a4.title: Education Statistics Digest 2025, Section 1 Table 4
web:95028705b6a4.finding: There were 237,966 primary students in 2024; this is the context population, not the number of buyers.
web:95028705b6a4.limitation: Counts students, not paying buyers. Table 2 and Table 4 disagree (230,968 vs 237,966). Says nothing about tuition centres.

web:1bfdc89eda0d.title: Singapore families spent S$1.8 billion on private tuition in 2023
web:1bfdc89eda0d.publisher: Malay Mail (citing Straits Times / SingStat household expenditure survey)
web:1bfdc89eda0d.quote: Families in Singapore reportedly spent S$1.8 billion (RM6 billion) on private tuition for their children in 2023
web:1bfdc89eda0d.finding: Households spend heavily on private tuition, so centres have paying customers; it does not show centres would buy diagnostic software.
web:1bfdc89eda0d.limitation: Secondary report; primary SingStat table not opened. All subjects and levels, not primary maths. Household spending on tuition, not centre spending on software.

web:4ee018643b7f.title: Online Education in Singapore: How Geniebook Supports Academic Success
web:4ee018643b7f.quote: AI-driven platforms like Geniebook tailor lessons based on students’ strengths and weaknesses, ensuring targeted improvement and better subject mastery.
web:4ee018643b7f.finding: The text shows that Geniebook provides AI-driven personalized lessons targeting student strengths and weaknesses.
web:4ee018643b7f.limitation: The quote does not explicitly state whether these reports are tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable, or sold specifically to tuition centres.

web:7a011e2fae32.title: The effect of a formative assessment practice on student achievement in mathematics
web:7a011e2fae32.quote: The 14 teachers who participated in the PDP taught a total of 291 students (the intervention group). The students belonging to this group were 148 females and 143 males. The remaining 15 teachers (6 females, 9 males) that taught year-7 mathematics that school year taught a total of 275 students (the control group).
web:7a011e2fae32.finding: The study evaluated mathematics achievement outcomes for 291 intervention students and 275 control students across participating secondary schools.
web:7a011e2fae32.limitation: The study measures general secondary mathematics achievement rather than specifically diagnosing primary mathematics learning gaps.

web:ce54a23ad257.title: Singapore's Education Ministry to deploy more AI in schools after success of primary 5 maths tool
web:ce54a23ad257.quote: launched the Adaptive Learning System for mathematics, for three topics covered at the Primary 5 level. That followed a pilot involving 33 schools that began last year. uses machine learning to make customised learning recommendations for each student.
web:ce54a23ad257.finding: The Singapore Education Ministry's Adaptive Learning System provides machine learning recommendations for primary mathematics students, but the text does not mention tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable learning-gap reports sold to tuition centres.
web:ce54a23ad257.limitation: The excerpt does not discuss commercial sales to tuition centres or whether reports are tutor-reviewed and evidence-traceable.

web:d15f8a509b69.title: Online Education in Singapore: How Geniebook Supports Academic Success
web:d15f8a509b69.quote: Parents receive detailed reports on their child’s strengths and areas for improvement, helping them provide timely support and keep learning on track.
web:d15f8a509b69.finding: The platform provides detailed reports on strengths and areas for improvement directly to parents.
web:d15f8a509b69.limitation: The text does not mention whether these reports are tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable, or sold specifically to tuition centres.
